Appearance:

Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for respondent No.2.
 Order

This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 12/08/2025 passed by I Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dhar (M.P.) in MACC No.534/2022, whereby an amount of Rs.7,88,000/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition to the appellants / claimants / survivors of the deceased Bhagwat Singh Rajput with interest @ 7% per annum.

entities.text: I Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dhar (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellants / survivors of the deceased submits that the learned Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month only.
At the time of accident deceased was owner of a Milk Dairy and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month for the milk business.
His contention is that as per the judgment delivered by the Apex Court in the case of Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr.

Vs. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9061 2 MA-8349-2025 Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093,
where the income of the deceased is not proved by any cogent evidence, income ought to have been assessed on the basis of circular issued by Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh under the Minimum Wages Act, according to which income of the deceased on the date of accident comes to Rs.11,360/- per month.

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On this ground, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance.

1 4.
Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

5. From perusal of the record, it is apparent that at the time of accident i.e. on 26/07/2022 deceased was owner of milk shop, however, his income has not been established by adducing cogent evidence,
therefore, in the light of the judgment in the case of Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram (Supra),
income of the deceased is to be assessed on the basis of circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act, therefore, on the basis of circular income of the deceased is taken as Rs.11,360/- per month considering him as 'Skilled NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9061 3 MA-8349-2025 Labourer'.
Adequate amount has been awarded in the other heads, therefore, the same needs no interference by this Court.

6. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
Loss of Dependency: Rs.11,360/- pm - 1/3rd PE x 12 Months x Multiplier of 7 =
Rs.6,36,160/-
 Loss of Consortium: Rs.1,92,000/-
 Loss of Estate: Rs.18,000/-
 Funeral Expenses: Rs.18,000/-
 Total Amount: Rs.8,64,160/-
 MACT Awarded: Rs.7,88,000/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.76,160/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.8,64,160/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.7,88,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.76,160/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellants / claimants is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.

Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest @ 7%
shall remain intact.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.
(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Tej Gulab Bai vs Mohammad Mohsin on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141848412/
